classification.difficultyReason: The student sums the sides of three shapes with two pronumerals, one of them an 8-sided shape, then matches each total to a factorised form. It is the same task as p9-q5 but with more sides and a 4(x+y) common-factor pattern. It needs no unknown-side reasoning like p9-q4.

content.prompt:
Match the shapes with the expressions that show their perimeters.

A. $4(x+y)$
B. $2(2x+y)$
C. $2(x+y)$

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}P_{\mathrm{i}}&=4x+4y\\P_{\mathrm{i}}&=4(x+y)\\P_{\mathrm{ii}}&=4x+2y\\P_{\mathrm{ii}}&=2(2x+y)\\P_{\mathrm{iii}}&=2x+2y\\P_{\mathrm{iii}}&=2(x+y)\end{align*}$$
The matches are i–A, ii–B and iii–C.
